day-1.t: Day 1 — What digital marketing really is

v: Know the four parts of digital marketing
Pick one clear goal for your business or page

b.v: About 20 minutes. Keep a notebook - by Day 10 you will have a full plan.

v: Content - posts, pictures, videos that people want to see
Search - being found when someone searches for what you sell
Ads - paying to show your message to the right people
Messages - chat, email and replies that turn interest into sales

b.v: Beginners try to do everything and finish nothing. Choose one goal for the next 30 days: more followers, more messages, more orders, or more visits to your website. Everything you post should help that one goal.

v: Weak: get famous
Strong: get 30 order messages a month from Lahore
Strong: grow the page from 200 to 600 followers by the end of next month

b.v: Do this now:|Write your one goal for the next 30 days.|Add a number and a date to it.|Write it on the first page of your notebook.

v: Describe your ideal customer in detail
Find what they worry about and want
Who: Ayesha, 28, teacher in Multan
Wants: affordable, decent clothes for work
Worries: online sellers who send poor quality
Where she spends time online: phone, evenings, short videos
What makes her buy: real photos, reviews from real buyers, cash on delivery

b.v: When you write a post, imagine you are talking only to Ayesha. Posts written for 'everyone' sound empty. Posts written for one real person feel personal, and many people like her respond.

v: Why did you buy from us?
What almost stopped you?
Where did you first see us?

b.v: Three honest answers from real buyers are worth more than a hundred guesses.
Do this now:|Make one customer card for your business.|Ask two real customers the three questions.|Update the card with their words.

v: Use content pillars so you never run out of ideas
Make a simple weekly plan

b.v: Pillars are 3 to 5 themes you post about again and again. For a home bakery: recipes and tips, behind the scenes, happy customers, new products and offers.
About 8 out of 10 posts should help, teach or entertain. Only about 2 out of 10 should directly sell. Pages that only sell get ignored.

v: Monday - a tip (teach)
Wednesday - behind the scenes (trust)
Friday - a customer story (proof)
Saturday - an offer (sell)

b.v: Four good posts a week beat fourteen rushed ones. Being regular matters more than being frequent.
Do this now:|Write 4 pillars for your business.|Plan next week's 4 posts in your notebook.|Take or collect the photos today.

day-4.t: Day 4 — Writing posts that get read

v: Write a strong first line (the hook)
Use the hook-problem-help-action shape

b.v: People see only the first one or two lines before 'See more'. That first line must make them stop scrolling: a question, a surprising fact, or a clear promise.

v: Still paying for a tailor every month? Here is how to measure at home.
We burned 40 cakes before we got this recipe right.
3 mistakes that make your shop look untrustworthy online.

b.v: Step by step:|Hook - stop the scroll|Problem - show you understand them|Help - your tip, story or product|Action - one clear next step: message us, visit the link, save this post
3) Easy to read on a phone

v: Short lines and blank lines between them
A few emojis as signposts, not in every word
One idea per post
English with a short Urdu line works well for Pakistani audiences

b.v: Do this now:|Write one post using the 4-step shape.|Read only the first line - would you stop for it?|Rewrite the hook three ways and choose the best.

v: Take clean product photos with a phone
Plan a 30-second video
Daylight near a window - no flash
Plain background: a white sheet or a wooden table
Clean the camera lens with a soft cloth
Show the product in use, not only on its own
Same style every time so your page looks like one brand
0-3 seconds: the hook, shown or said
3-25 seconds: show the process, the result or the tip
25-30 seconds: the action - 'message us to order'
Add subtitles - many people watch with the sound off

b.v: XpertCreation's Video Translate can make subtitles for your video in Urdu or English, and XpertCam has filters for quick edits.
Do not use songs or clips you do not have the rights to. Platforms mute or remove such videos, and repeated strikes can close your page.
Do this now:|Take 5 photos of one product using the list above.|Pick the best one.|Plan a 30-second video on paper using the four parts.

day-6.t: Day 6 — Getting found on search (SEO basics)

v: Understand keywords
Make your page and listings easy to find

b.v: 1) Keywords are the words people type
People do not search for your brand name - they search for what they need: 'bridal makeup in Gujranwala', 'cheap laptop repair near me', 'home tutor maths class 9'. These are keywords.

v: Your page name and short description
Product titles: 'Cotton lawn suit, 3 piece, unstitched' beats 'New arrival!!'
The first line of your posts and listings
Picture names and descriptions on your website
Add your shop to online maps with the exact address, phone and opening hours
Ask happy real customers to leave an honest review
Keep the same name, address and phone everywhere

b.v: Never buy or write fake reviews. It is dishonest, platforms remove them and can ban the business.
Do this now:|Write 10 keywords your customers would type.|Rewrite three product titles using them.|Check your shop's map listing is correct.

day-7.t: Day 7 — Paid ads on a small budget

v: Know how a basic ad works
Run a small test before spending more

b.v: 1) The three choices in every ad

v: Goal - messages, website visits, followers or video views
Audience - city, age, interests (use your customer card from Day 2)
Budget and time - for example Rs 500 a day for 5 days

b.v: Run two versions of the same ad with different pictures or hooks, each with a small budget. After 3 to 5 days keep the one that brought more messages for less money, and stop the other.

v: Choosing 'everyone in Pakistan' as the audience
Boosting a post with no clear next step
Changing the ad every few hours - give it a few days
Spending a big budget before testing

b.v: On XpertCreation you can boost a post, profile, shop or listing from the Promote page and see views and clicks.
Do this now:|Write two hooks for the same offer.|Choose the city and age of your audience.|Decide your test budget and stopping date before you start.

v: Reply fast and well
Build trust that leads to orders

b.v: A customer who asks 'price?' and gets an answer in 5 minutes often buys. Two days later they have already bought from someone else. Set times in the day when you answer all messages.

v: Greet, answer the question, then ask one question back: 'Which size do you need?'
Give the full price including delivery - no surprises
Send a real photo or short video of the actual item
Make ordering easy: name, address, phone, payment method
Real photos of real orders (with the customer's permission)
Clear return and exchange policy
A verified company page on XpertCreation
Cash on delivery for first-time buyers

b.v: Do this now:|Write saved replies for your 5 most common questions.|Write your return policy in 3 lines.|Pin it on your page.

v: Know which numbers matter
Decide what to do more of and less of
Reach - how many people saw it
Engagement - likes, comments, shares, saves
Clicks or messages - people who took the next step
Sales - the number that pays the bills
Cost per message or order - for ads

b.v: Likes feel good but do not always mean sales. A post with 50 likes and 10 orders is better than one with 500 likes and no orders. Judge posts by your goal from Day 1.
Step by step:|Write down last week's best and worst post.|Ask why the best one worked: the hook, the picture, the time, the topic?|Do more of that next week, and drop what did not work.
Keep a simple table in Excel or any spreadsheet: date, post topic, reach, messages, orders.
Do this now:|Look at your last 10 posts.|Find the one with the most messages or sales.|Plan 2 posts like it for next week.

v: Put everything into one plan you can follow
Start today
Goal with a number and a date (Day 1)
Customer card (Day 2)
4 content pillars and a weekly plan (Day 3)
Keywords for titles (Day 6)
A small ad test (Day 7)
Saved replies and return policy (Day 8)
Weekly review every Sunday (Day 9)
Real photos, real reviews, real prices
No fake followers or bought likes
Credit other people's photos and music, or do not use them
